text:
jen: Heads up — customers reporting they can SSO in but audit shows unexpected role flips to 'admin' for a tiny subset. Not a full exploit but noisy for compliance. Anyone seeing related deploys?
kevin: Not seeing deploys from infra this morning. Which idp? Okta or AAD?
jen: Okta tenant A. Problem looks tied to SAML assertion parsing on our side. Saw this in one audit row: 
```
SAML_ATTR: {\"roles\":\"[\\\"user\\\",\\\"admin\\\"]\"}, subject: user|extid:12345, kmd: KMS-v2
```
jen: Note roles is a JSON-string inside the attribute instead of proper array. Our parser treats comma as separator and ends up mapping to both user+admin.
olga: oh - some partners send roles as a JSON blob in the attribute instead of multiple attrs. We normalized that recently in scim-sync pipeline? Could be the new RBAC mapping change that trimmed whitespace.
kevin: I recall a small RBAC mapping change rolled last week to coerce roles string -> list. That code path uses lib-claimparser v1.3.0. Did we rewrap keys with KMS last week?
sam: infra-bot shows a KMS rewrap activity at 1712480000 for key alias kms/claims-enc (recent rotation). That might have coincided. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/sso-claims-parsing
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled lib-claimparser@1.3.0 to svc-auth at 1712499000 by kevin-deploy.
jen: ok that lines up. So theory: new lib coerces JSON-string -> split then we treat bracketed role string as two comma-separated values including an empty token that maps to admin? (weird).
kevin: Can you paste minimal repro from logs?
jen: here's sanitized repro from service logs: 
```
Received SAML attrs: roles=\"[\\\"user\\\",\\\"admin\\\"]\"
claimparser.normalize(roles) -> [\"[\\\"user\\\"\",\"\\\"admin\\\"]\"]
rbac.map_roles(normalized) -> grant: user, admin
```
jen: So the normalize step is splitting on comma without unquoting JSON string. Bug.
olga: Mitigation: revert lib-claimparser or patch normalize to detect JSON array string and json.parse it. Short-term: revert mapping change (canary) or add an allowlist to ignore roles that start with '['.
sam: Oncall window: we can hotfix mapping in config to ignore JSON-like strings. I can push a config roll to prod-safe route 2 in 5m if owners ok.
kevin: +1 to config flag. Also need to check audit logs for any admin actions performed by those elevated sessions. Jen, can you run a quick query and list any admin API calls between 1712400000-1712550000? Use the internal query: 
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" "https://audit-api.internal/query?since=1712400000&until=1712550000&filter=role:admin"
```
jen: running that now, will paste results.
jen: small set (~6) of user-scoped changes, nothing escalatory (no key deletions), still need full review. Punting to vuln-triage later but priority is to stop further noisy grants.
olga: After config patch, add a unit test for JSON-string attributes. Also update SCIM transformation docs — some IdPs send JSON in a single attr by design.
kevin: I'll open a quick PR to add detection: if attr matches /^\s*\[.*\]\s*$/ then JSON.parse before split. Ship in canary.
sam: Can we also add an audit alert for any future role mapping changes that newly grant admin? Create an alert rule: "rbac_mapped_admin_new" -> page security-oncall.
jen: created alert ticket INC-4532, linking to this thread.
infra-bot: alert-config-bot: Created rule rbac_mapped_admin_new -> severity: high, notify: security-oncall.
jen: rolling config change now to disable claimparser coercion on prod; will monitor for 10m.
kevin: after you confirm, I'll revert lib if needed.
jen: 10m monitor in progress — no new admin mappings in that window. :thumbsup:
sam: follow-up tasks: PR for parsing fix, unit tests, update runbooks, scan audit trail for the 6 events (assign to olga).
olga: ACK, will take audit review and SCIM doc update.
jen: thanks all. Postmortem + timeline after full audit. Leaving thread open for vuln-triage notes.
